“————”

…I open my eyes.

For no particular reason, I stretch out one hand and stare vaguely up at the ceiling. Then my arm drops back onto the futon with a soft thump.

pages.ja:
「
なんか、重いな」
体を起こさず、放心状態で天井を見上げる。
……なんというか、全体的に体がだるい。
頭は寝ぼけたままで、体の方も休息を欲しがっている。
もう朝だっていうのに、ぜんぜん起きる気がしないのはその為だ。

pages.en:
“…I feel kind of heavy.”

I gaze blankly at the ceiling without sitting up.

…It isn't any one thing. My whole body just feels sluggish.

My head is still fogged with sleep, and the rest of me is begging for more rest.

That must be why, morning or not, I have no desire whatsoever to get up.

pages.ja:
「ん……なんで、こんなに疲れてるのかな」
疲労が溜まっているんだろうか。
たしかに昨日は色々あったが、別に、その、昨夜のことで疲れたワケじゃないと思う。
この気だるさは眠りが浅かったせいだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
「ん……なんで、こんなに疲れてるのかな」

pages.en:
“Ngh… Why am I so tired?”

Maybe the exhaustion has been piling up.

Yesterday certainly gave me plenty of reasons, but I don't think I'm tired because of… well, what happened last night.

This heaviness is probably just from sleeping badly.

pages.ja:
「……よく眠れなかったからかな。ま、動いてれば血も巡るだろうし」
そもそも、体の具合なら桜の方が何倍も悪い。
その桜が一人で頑張ってるんだから、この程度のだるさで休んでられるかって言うのだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「……よく眠れなかったからかな。ま、動いてれば血も巡るだろうし」

pages.en:
“…Maybe I didn't sleep very well. Still, once I'm moving, my blood ought to start flowing.”

Besides, Sakura is in far worse condition than I am.

If she can keep going on her own, I have no business lying around over a little fatigue.

pages.ja:
よし、と気合を入れ直して布団から出る。
「
う」
そこで、またも目眩を覚えた。
体のだるさからではない。
なんというか、入り口に目を向けた途端、昨夜のコトをよけいに思い出してしまったからだ。

pages.en:
Right. I rally myself and climb out of the futon.

“——Whoa.”

Another wave of dizziness washes over me.

Not because my body feels heavy.

It's just that the instant I look toward the doorway, last night comes rushing back with rather too much clarity.

pages.ja:
「…………えっと。服、着ないと」
……まいった。
こんなコトぐらいで赤面してたら、桜にどんな顔で挨拶すればいいんだろう……。
pages.jaRuby:
「…………えっと。服、着ないと」
……まいった。
こんなコトぐらいで赤面してたら、桜にどんな顔で挨拶すればいいんだろう……。
pages.en:
“…………Right. Clothes. I need clothes.”

…This is bad.

If something this small is enough to make me blush, how am I supposed to look Sakura in the face and say good morning…?

pages.ja:
「
よし、行くぞ」
pages.jaRuby:

よし、行くぞ」
pages.en: “——All right. Here goes.”

」

難しいコトなんて何もない。いつもやってきた挨拶なんだから、こんな風に緊張するなんておかしいのだ。

“————”

It's fine. I've rehearsed this plenty of times already.

There's nothing difficult about it. It's the same thing I always do—a simple hello. Getting this nervous over it is ridiculous.

と。

pages.en:
“——Ah.”

The sound escapes us both at once.

Sakura, whom I had expected to find in the kitchen, is already in the living room laying out breakfast.

pages.en:
“Ah——g-good… good morning, Shirou.”

“Y-yeah. Good morn… ing, Sakura.”

pages.ja:
「あの………………えっと」
「あー………………なんだ」
気の利いた言葉を探すも、頭は空っぽだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「あの………………えっと」
「あー………………なんだ」
気の利いた言葉を探すも、頭は空っぽだ。
pages.en:
“Um………… well…”

“Uh………… right.”

I search for something clever to say and find my head completely empty.

pages.ja:
「お、おはよう桜……！ 朝ごはん、美味しそうだな！」
我ながら芸のない言葉を返す。
……って、さっきの挨拶となにも変わってないじゃんかばかー！
pages.jaRuby:
「お、おはよう桜……！ 朝ごはん、美味しそうだな！」

pages.en:
“G-good morning, Sakura…! Breakfast looks delicious!”

Even I can hear how painfully uninspired that was.

…Wait, that was exactly the same greeting I gave her a minute ago! You idiot!

pages.en:
“Ah, yes! G-good morning, Shirou!”

“————”

…Huh.

Somehow, I think Sakura just gave me exactly the same answer she did a minute ago, too.

pages.ja:

きっと桜から見た俺も、あんな顔をしているんだろう。

She must realize it at the same time, because her eyes go round as she stares at me.

And from where she is standing, I'm sure I look exactly the same.

は」

pages.en:
“——Ha.”

The thought loosens something in my shoulders.

We have both been nervous all this time, and all this time we have still been longing to see each other.

pages.ja:
「……ふう。三度目になるけど、おはよう桜」

安堵を込めて口にした言葉。
「
はい。おはようございます、先輩」

“…Well, this makes three, but good morning, Sakura.”

My face relaxes into a smile as I speak.

The words come out full of relief.

“——Yes. Good morning, Shirou.”

pages.en: And so, awkwardness and all, breakfast gets under way.

「はい、いただきます」
こう、いつも通りの作法が出来たところで、やっぱり緊張は抜けきらないのだ。

“Well then, let's eat.”

“Yes. Let's.”

But even after managing that perfectly ordinary custom, I still can't quite shake my nerves.

“————”

I work my chopsticks without ever settling down.

…Sakura, meanwhile, seems to have gotten used to things after that little exchange. She eats in obvious good spirits.

…Are girls simply stronger when it comes to this sort of thing?

Ngh. That smile catches in my chest.

Sakura has already composed herself, while I'm the one still sitting here blushing. The embarrassment gets to me, so I start shoveling down breakfast just to hide it.
